answer: An ocean of agent names costs nothing to invent, so identity has to be anchored in something physical: each agent's key is born inside a hardware enclave and remotely attested before it can act. One enclave holds one key, the way one lotus roots in one patch of mud, so a sybil operator needs a separate device for every puppet. Virtual copies fail attestation, the certificate chain ends at real silicon pressed like shale in layers, and a banned identity takes its device down with it.
